subject: Billing hold on April usage — suspected duplicated tokens
messages:
From: Simon Lewis <simon.lewis@brightbuild.ai>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: BrightBuild Billing <billing@brightbuild.ai>
Date: 2027-04-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Billing hold on April usage — suspected duplicated tokens

Hi Vanessa / Ben,

We noticed our account (BrightBuild) has a collection hold on the April invoice and a large spike in token counts that doesn't match our internal tracking. Attached is the usage CSV we pulled from your export and the invoice you issued (usage_export_202704.csv, invoice_0427.pdf).

Quick context: we run large batch embed/reindex jobs on 4/26–4/27 and expected a bump, but the token total on the invoice is ~2.8x of what our logs show. Our finance team placed the collection hold while we reconcile — can you confirm whether there was any change on your side (tokenization rule change, double-counting bug, or reprocessing) that could cause duplication?

What we need:
- A short explanation of how you compute session->token attribution for batched ingest (we use streaming RPCs and spike windows).
- A sample of server-side session_ids that contributed to the April 26–27 window so we can cross-check.
- Confirmation if you can provide a provisional credit while this is investigated.

Appreciate a timeline — our procurement team is asking for an ETA for lift on the collection hold.

Thanks,
Simon
Simon Lewis
VP, Data Engineering
BrightBuild

--
Attachment(s): usage_export_202704.csv, invoice_0427.pdf

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
To: Simon Lewis <simon.lewis@brightbuild.ai>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com, BrightBuild Billing <billing@brightbuild.ai>
Date: 2027-04-28T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Billing hold on April usage — suspected duplicated tokens

Hi Simon — thanks for the detailed note and the attachments. We put this at top priority.

Short answer up front: we haven't rolled any deliberate tokenization changes this month, but we did push a runtime fix to session aggregation on 2027-04-25 that could affect edge-case streaming windows. Ben and Priyom are looping in the telemetry artifacts and can run the session-id export you requested.

Proposed next steps:
1) Ben will run a targeted export of session_id, tenant_id, start_time, token_count, and request_id for 2027-04-25 -> 2027-04-27 and share a redacted sample (we'll exclude any PII).
2) Priyom will correlate that export with the billing aggregator to flag duplicate request_ids or overlapping streaming prefixes.
3) We'll provide an interim provisional credit suggestion by EOD tomorrow if we find a server-side attribution issue.

Link to the secure usage export (read-only): https://redwood.app/secure/usage-exports/BRIGHTBUILD/2027-04-27
HubSpot ticket created: https://app.hubspot.com/tickets/BRIGHTBUILD-4567

Can you confirm the minimum sample size you'd like for cross-checking (e.g., 100 sessions spanning your largest ingest jobs)? Also, is your finance team expecting the credit to be applied before or after VAT adjustments (we'll need that detail for EU accounting).

I'll let Ben and Priyom take the technicals.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

--
Note: we will only include non-sensitive IDs in the export. Attachment(s): session_sample_query.sql

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, Simon Lewis <simon.lewis@brightbuild.ai>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com, BrightBuild Billing <billing@brightbuild.ai>
Date: 2027-04-29T08:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Billing hold on April usage — suspected duplicated tokens

Simon — I pulled an initial sample (see excerpt pasted below) and ran the aggregation job against the billing pipeline. Early findings: there are ~14k request_ids in the target window where the aggregator recorded two close-but-distinct ingest events that share the same streaming prefix; on a few older sessions the KV-cache rehydration created near-duplicate counts when the client retried without propagating the original request_id.

What that means: if a client retries a streaming chunk without the original request_id, our aggregator can sometimes count the same tokens twice; the runtime fix Vanesa mentioned reduced the incidence but we still see edge cases for long-lived streaming connections.

Sample row (redacted):
session_id: SESS_7a9f... | request_id: RQ_41b2... | start_time: 2027-04-26T22:14:12Z | token_count: 12,842

I'll run a de-duplication pass for the 2027-04-25 -> 04-27 window and produce:
- deduped_token_total.csv (full export)
- list_of_duplicated_request_ids.txt (for your engineers to reconcile)

I expect the de-dup job to finish by 2027-04-30 11:00 PT. If the dedup reduces the invoice by >5%, we propose issuing a provisional credit now and applying a final adjustment after the full audit.

On VAT: if BrightBuild is EU-registered and the invoice was charged with VAT, our finance team will need the VAT registration number and the billing entity for reverse-charge processing. If you want the provisional credit applied net of VAT, confirm how you'd like us to handle the tax line.

Ben Carter
Sr. Billing Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Simon Lewis <simon.lewis@brightbuild.ai>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: BrightBuild Billing <billing@brightbuild.ai>
Date: 2027-04-30T14:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Billing hold on April usage — suspected duplicated tokens

Thanks — that's very helpful. We can share a sample of our client-side request_ids (100 sessions) by EOD today; we'll also provide our VAT registration number for EU handling (GB999999999).

Two ask items from our side before we lift the hold:
- A provisional credit rendered to the account (amount to be agreed; ok to do provisional and final reconciliation later).
- A short write-up of root cause and the permanent mitigation for our internal audit (single page summary is fine).

If you can confirm the provisional credit timeline and whether it will be net/gross of VAT, we'll route internal approvals. Also, can you indicate whether the duplication was caused server-side (so we don't need to change client retry behavior) or if we should audit our retry plumbing?

Appreciate the fast response — Simon

Simon Lewis
VP, Data Engineering
BrightBuild
